sections.html:
Montgomery, on the Alabama River, is the state capital and the seat of Montgomery County. It had 200,603 residents in 2020. Government work, Maxwell-Gunter Air Force Base, healthcare and manufacturing give the market a steadier base than a single-industry town, though sellers still run into the usual problems: inherited houses, rentals and older homes that need work.

Countywide there were 105,293 housing units in 2020, and 11.5% were vacant, so empty houses are a normal part of the market. Owners live in 56.3% of occupied homes and renters in 43.7%. Many sellers are therefore landlords with rentals that may carry back taxes.

Hope Hull and Pike Road are the only towns besides Montgomery. A seller in an unincorporated community such as Pintlala, Snowdoun or Mount Meigs deals with the same county Revenue Commissioner as a seller downtown. Montgomery Public Schools serves most of the county, while Pike Road has its own school district.

sections.h2: Who bills the tax and when
sections.html:
The Montgomery County Revenue Commissioner assesses and bills property tax for houses in the city. Tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. From there the state timetable runs to the probate court in February, a newspaper advertisement in April and a tax sale in May.

Notices of value come from the county Board of Equalization, so look for yours in the spring and read it the day it arrives. The clock for an appeal starts from the date printed on it, not from the day you open it.

Send a request to the county, with supporting documents, within 30 days of the date printed on your notice. The county charges no fee, requires no form, and offers an informal review before the Board of Equalization that it recommends.

Appeal detailWhat to know
Deadline30 days from the date printed on the notice
FeeNone
Where to send itpropertytaxappeals@mc-ala.org
Phone, real property appeals(334) 832-1327
Helpful documentsClosing statements, appraisals, comparable sales, insurance values

The board wants all supporting documents filed with the appeal and asks for original signatures. An out-of-state representative can file for an owner. An attorney is not required, but the representative must supply a signed authorization form.

After a board ruling, state law gives 30 days to appeal to circuit court under Alabama Code 40-3-25. You must keep paying prior-year taxes on time while the case continues.

The board decides on paper, so the file matters. Closing statements from recent nearby sales show what buyers actually paid. An appraisal done for a refinance or a purchase gives a professional opinion of value. Insurance values show what it would cost to rebuild. Photos and repair estimates explain why your house is worth less than a similar one down the street.

Label every page with your name and the parcel number, sign the originals, and keep a copy of everything you send. If you ask for the informal review first, you may settle the matter before it ever reaches the board, and you lose nothing by trying.

Summers are long and hot, with highs above 90 degrees on about 86 days a year and heat indexes often at or above 100. Spring thunderstorms can bring large hail, damaging wind and tornado risk, and tropical systems that weaken inland can drop very heavy rain.

For a house, that makes the roof the first thing an inspector will look at, followed by drainage and the air conditioning unit. Substantial snowstorms happen roughly once every ten years, so freeze damage is a lesser concern than heat and storms. A cash buyer will take the house with a tired roof or an old air conditioner as it is.

A Montgomery deed is recorded with the probate judge, and Alabama Code 40-22-1 requires the recording privilege tax of $0.50 per $500 of value before the deed is accepted. The deed has to come with a form stating the real purchase price.

Unpaid property tax, if any, comes out of the seller's proceeds, handled by the title company.

  • Request a payoff figure from the Revenue Commissioner.
  • Collect the deed, the closing statement and any survey.
  • File the deed with the probate judge after closing.
  • New owners should assess the house in their own name.

With more than four in ten occupied homes rented, a Montgomery sale often involves a tenant. Read the lease for its end date and for any clause about showings. Tell the tenant what is happening before a stranger knocks on the door.

Landlords also tend to be the owners with older tax years open. Ask the Revenue Commissioner whether more than one year is unpaid, because each year gets its own advertising and fees once the account is delinquent. Pay the oldest year first if you are paying in pieces, and keep every receipt.

A cash buyer can often close with the tenant still in place or with the house empty, whichever you prefer. Say which you want when you ask for an offer.

Back taxes do not block a sale. The Revenue Commissioner gives a payoff figure, the title company pays it from your proceeds, and you receive the rest. A payoff figure is only good for the date it was calculated, so the closer may ask for an updated one if the closing moves. Act before the sale calendar reaches April, when parcels are advertised, and ideally before January, when the account becomes delinquent.

If you are appealing a value and plan to sell during the appeal, settle that question with your closing attorney first, since the appeal rules require prior-year taxes to stay current.

Montgomery sellers often hold inherited houses, rentals or older homes that need work. Cash Home Buyers buys Montgomery houses as is, including those with back taxes, and the title company pays any unpaid property tax from the proceeds. No lender is involved, so there is no appraisal to pass and no repair list to answer.

Before you call a buyer or an agent, pull the deed and your latest tax notice, and ask the Revenue Commissioner whether anything is owed. For an inherited house, bring whatever shows who holds title now.

faqs.q: Who sends Montgomery, Alabama property tax bills?
faqs.a: The Montgomery County Revenue Commissioner assesses and bills property tax for houses inside the city of Montgomery.

faqs.q: When is Montgomery property tax due?
faqs.a: Property tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Montgomery property value?
faqs.a: You have 30 days from the date printed on your notice, and the county says there is no filing fee.

faqs.q: What documents help a Montgomery appeal?
faqs.a: The county names closing statements, appraisals, comparable sales and insurance values as examples, and the board wants them filed with the appeal.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Montgomery house that has unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is paid from the proceeds at closing, so get a payoff figure from the Revenue Commissioner first.
